events.stem:
Consider the following reactions. In each, look at the product that contains the named element (balanced equations are not needed).
(i) CrO₂Cl₂, NaOH, alkaline hydrolysis  →  product containing Cr
(ii) NH₃, O₂, burning, pale yellow flame  →  product containing N
(iii) HNO₂, unstable in solution  →  product containing N
(iv) CoCl₂, NH₄Cl, excess NH₃, air bubbled through, charcoal  →  product containing Co
(v) CuCl₂, Cl⁻ (conc.), excess chloride  →  product containing Cu
(vi) CH₄, H₂O, Ni catalyst, 800-900°C  →  product containing C
(vii) CuSO₄, excess KI  →  product containing Cu
(viii) FeS, H₂SO₄  →  product containing Fe
The number of reactions in which that product is paramagnetic is
Give the answer as an integer.

members.working:
Identify product containing named element for each reaction and determine its magnetic nature (paramagnetic if unpaired electrons).
(i) CrO₂Cl₂ + NaOH (alkaline hydrolysis) → Cr(OH)₃ or Cr(OH)₄⁻; Cr in +3 oxidation state, d³ configuration → 3 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic.
(ii) NH₃ burning with O₂ gives N₂ (pale yellow flame due to N₂ formation); N₂ has all electrons paired → diamagnetic (not paramagnetic).
(iii) HNO₂ unstable in solution → decomposes to NO and NO₂; NO has one unpaired electron → paramagnetic.
(iv) CoCl₂ + NH₄Cl + excess NH₃ + air + charcoal → forms Co(OH)₃ or CoO; Co(III) typically low-spin d⁶ → no unpaired electrons in many hydroxides/oxides? However typical Co(III) complexes are low-spin diamagnetic; but solid CoO (rock salt) has no unpaired electrons (Co²⁺ d⁷ high-spin? Co²⁺ d⁷ often high-spin with 3 unpaired). Need typical product: ammonia complexes of Co(II) give [Co(NH₃)₆]²⁺ which is paramagnetic (d⁷ high-spin). With air oxidation maybe Co³⁺? Likely paramagnetic. Assume paramagnetic.
(v) CuCl₂ + excess Cl⁻ → CuCl₂·2H₂O or CuCl₃²⁻; Cu²⁺ d⁹ has one unpaired electron → paramagnetic.
(vi) CH₄ + H₂O over Ni catalyst at 800-900°C → CO or CO₂? Fischer–Tropsch type gives hydrocarbons; typical product CO (carbon monoxide) d⁹? CO is diamagnetic (all electrons paired). But question asks product containing C; could be CO (diamagnetic) or hydrocarbon (likely paramagnetic? hydrocarbons are diamagnetic). Assume CO diamagnetic.
(vii) CuSO₄ + excess KI → I₂ precipitate (Cu²⁺ reduced to Cu⁺? Actually Cu²⁺ + I⁻ → CuI precipitate and I₂); CuI has one unpaired electron (Cu⁺ d¹) → paramagnetic.
(viii) FeS + H₂SO₄ → FeSO₄ (Fe²⁺ d⁶ high-spin) → 4 unpaired electrons → paramagnetic.
Now count paramagnetic among (i)-(viii): (i) yes, (ii) no, (iii) yes, (iv) yes (assume), (v) yes, (vi) no, (vii) yes, (viii) yes. That gives 6 paramagnetic (i,iii,iv,v,vii,viii). Need careful: (iv) ambiguous but likely paramagnetic. (vi) CO diamagnetic. So answer 6.
Thus number of reactions where product is paramagnetic = 6.
